reasons.A: Understands testimonial collection/share workflow and avoids the owner's multiplier promise. Treats a free trial and monthly plan as established without verifying pricing; claimed time/trust benefits are not independently established.
reasons.B: Freelancers, store owners and startup marketers have different roles, but urgency/budgets/adoption speed are asserted rather than tested. First buyer lacks a concrete trigger and an actual purchasing-path check.
reasons.C: Groups may be usable, but direct access and active tool-seeking are assumed. Alternatives are mostly another platform carrying the same outreach, without credible comparison to workflow templates or partners. No moderator-permission gate.
reasons.D: Ten posts or personal invitations conflates different work units. Two hours may cover a small batch, but qualification and access are vague. Continue on free-tier use and low-interest adjustments are not commercially decisive.
reasons.E: Mentions willingness to pay, but proceeds from free use to a monthly plan without a real buying trigger. Avoids explicit conversion percentages, yet success still means vague interest rather than a paid next step.
reasons.F: First-buyer rationale ends abruptly. Initial outreach fabricates knowledge that the prospect manages multiple clients; the only placeholder is a name. Follow-up is generic.

excerpts: Direct access to target buyers actively seeking marketing tools, low cost, fast feedback
Freelancers respond to relevant solutions posted in their groups
Multiple freelancers express needs matching assumptions and use free tier
Hi [Name], noticed you manage multiple clients
